page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6t.26xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processors running at a base clock frequency of 2.5 GHz on x86_64 architecture. The server provides 104 dedicated virtual central processing units (vCPUs) and 192.0 GB of RAM. This configuration yields a memory-to-vCPU ratio of approximately 1.85 GB per core, prioritizing raw CPU processing thread density over high memory capacities per execution thread.

The instance operates under a KVM hypervisor architecture and features a baseline network bandwidth capacity of 32 Gbps to handle distributed network communications. The instance does not include bundled local disk storage or dedicated GPU accelerators, requiring external network block storage for persistent data and operating system requirements.

With 104 dedicated cores and a focused memory allocation, the hardware profile offers strong multi-core computational density for parallel processing. The primary trade-off is the lack of onboard NVMe storage and relatively tight RAM per vCPU, making it less suitable for memory-intensive caching layers or massive databases. It provides efficient compute resource utilization for CPU-bound enterprise workloads, including batch calculations, multi-threaded compilation pipelines, continuous integration systems, and distributed Web application microservices.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6t.26xlarge is a high-density compute-optimized virtual server instance based on the x86_64 architecture and managed via KVM hypervisors. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz, the instance delivers 104 dedicated vCPUs alongside 192.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a ratio of 1.85 GB of RAM per vCPU core. The server lacks onboard local storage drives and dedicated GPU hardware, depending on attached network block storage for persistent disk access. Network capabilities are defined by a 32 Gbps baseline bandwidth ceiling. The compute-heavy hardware balance makes this instance appropriate for CPU-intensive parallel processing, batch computing jobs, software build clusters, high-concurrency microservices, and mathematical simulations where processing thread density takes precedence over large per-core memory footprints or local disk IOPS requirements.
